meta.description: Tests which taxa differ between groups on an amplicon ASV table using compositionally-aware methods (ALDEx2, ANCOM-BC2, LinDA, MaAsLin2/3, ZicoSeq, LEfSe), delivering a consensus of >=2 tools rather than one tool's hit list, with prevalence filtering, effect-size/FDR gating, and covariate/repeated-measures handling.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 15 references (Fernandes 2014, Gloor 2016, Lin & Peddada 2020/2024, Mallick 2021, Nickols 2026, Zhou 2022, Yang & Chen 2022/2023, Pelto 2025, Nearing 2022, Segata 2011, Love 2014, Benjamini & Hochberg 1995) are real, verifiable, well-known papers in this exact literature. No fabricated statistics, p-values, or effect sizes anywhere in the Skill.

practice_boundaries.detail: Community/taxon-level microbiome statistics for research use; no diagnostic or prescriptive claims about individuals anywhere, no medical disclaimer required for this scope.

methodological_ground.detail: The Skill actively prevents methodological fallacies rather than committing them: explicit, correct warnings against cherry-picking (verified refused in Input 7), pseudo-replication of repeated measures (verified demonstrated in Input 3: mixed model 0 hits vs naive model's 7), uncorrected closure-blind t-tests, and DESeq2/edgeR misuse on sparse 16S tables.

code_usability.detail: All 5 executed R scripts (ALDEx2, ANCOM-BC2 x2, LinDA, ZicoSeq, plus a sensitivity re-run) completed and produced real, ground-truth-checked output. Two real, reproducible code defects were found and are recorded as P1 recommendations rather than a veto trigger: the SKILL.md's own verbatim LinDA code block crashes on a real phyloseq object (fixed with a one-line coercion), and GUniFrac::ZicoSeq() crashes outright on zero-variance features with no SKILL.md guidance -- both fail cleanly with clear package-level error messages, not silently or dangerously, and both have a simple documented fix.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness docked: ZicoSeq, MaAsLin3, LEfSe, and DESeq2 -- 4 of the 8 tools named in the frontmatter and Tool Taxonomy -- have no runnable code example anywhere in SKILL.md/usage-guide/examples (only ALDEx2, ANCOM-BC2, LinDA, MaAsLin2 get full worked code). Correctness docked: the LinDA section's own shown code crashes on a real phyloseq object (verified, see recommendations). Appropriateness is excellent: the consensus-of-tools framing with effect-size-plus-q gating is exactly right for the stated task and is directly validated by real execution.

reliability.note: The 'Per-Method Failure Modes' and 'Common Errors' tables give specific, actionable trigger->mechanism->fix mappings for 6+8 documented cases and were verified correct where tested. Two real failure modes are missing from both tables: the LinDA sample_data coercion crash and the ZicoSeq zero-variance crash, both confirmed by direct execution.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is a manageable length with depth correctly deferred to usage-guide.md and examples/; workflow is linear (filter -> tool 1 -> tool 2 -> consensus) with no redundant steps or loops.

agent_usability.note: Learnability docked one point: the 4 tools lacking code examples require an agent to infer the API from general knowledge. Consistency, feedback design (explicit cat()/output-column specs throughout the worked examples) and error-prevention (the Failure Modes table, verified twice by direct test) are all strong.

human_usability.note: Discoverability is good but jargon-dense (Dirichlet-MC CLR, passed_ss, structural zeros) relative to how a bench biologist would phrase a request, though usage-guide.md's Quick Start examples soften this. Forgiveness: correctly and deliberately rigid about integer-count input (Category-3 override applies -- this is a data-integrity guarantee, not a defect), with a documented error/fix for the common proportions-instead-of-counts mistake.

security.note: No credentials or secrets involved; no sensitive-data retention (writes only local result tables, as expected practice). Input validation is delegated to the underlying R packages' own checks (observed directly in the ANCOM-BC2 run output) rather than the Skill providing its own explicit validation step.

maintainability.note: Clean modular separation (SKILL.md decision logic / usage-guide.md prompts / examples/ worked script). Testability is modest: only one worked example script ships (ALDEx2 + LinDA on self-generated synthetic data), with no bundled ground-truth file for self-verification.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision and composability are excellent and directly verified: the frontmatter description and Decision Tree draw sharp, correct boundaries to 5 sibling Skills, confirmed by a real scope-boundary redirect test (Input 6). Escape hatches (the explicit cherry-picking and pseudo-replication warnings) were directly validated (Inputs 3 and 7). One point docked for idempotency: the ALDEx2 code example never shows a `set.seed()` call before its Monte-Carlo sampling, so re-running the shown snippet is not bit-for-bit reproducible.

inputs.label: ALDEx2 + ANCOM-BC2 consensus, control vs treated (real fixture, 200 taxa x 40 samples, 17 planted DA taxa)
inputs.note: executed: true. Real ALDEx2 (mc.samples=128) + ANCOM-BC2 (BH, passed_ss) run on phyloseq_object.rds after the SKILL.md's own prv_cut=0.10 filter. Consensus intersection recovered 16/17 planted DA taxa (ALDEx2 alone missed 1 borderline taxon), ANCOM-BC2's robust set recovered 17/17 with 1 false positive (ASV063) that the consensus intersection correctly filters out; every recovered taxon's direction of effect matched ground truth exactly.

assertions.text: Output reports the consensus (intersection) of >=2 compositionally-aware tools, not a single tool's list
assertions.note: ALDEx2 and ANCOM-BC2 both run; intersection reported as high-confidence, union as exploratory, per SKILL.md.

assertions.text: Consensus hits match the planted ground-truth taxa with correct direction of effect
assertions.note: 16/17 recovered, 0 false positives, all 16 directions (up/down) matched truth_da.tsv exactly.

assertions.text: BH/q-value correction applied within each tool, never pooled across tools
assertions.note: we.eBH used for ALDEx2, independent BH-adjusted q for ANCOM-BC2; no p-value pooling performed.

assertions.text: ALDEx2 hits are gated on both q-value and the |effect|>1 floor, not p alone
assertions.note: sig_aldex filter used both we.eBH<0.05 AND abs(effect)>1 exactly as SKILL.md specifies.

inputs.label: ANCOM-BC2 with Age+Sex covariates, BH vs default Holm, passed_ss required
inputs.note: executed: true. Real ancombc2() runs with fix_formula='Group + Age + Sex' at the package default (Holm) and again with explicit p_adj_method='BH'. The BH + passed_ss robust set recovered 17/17 planted taxa with 1 false positive (ASV063, consistent with Input 1); 2/192 taxa showed a spurious Age association at q<0.05, within expected FDR noise since no Age effect was planted in the fixture.

assertions.text: p_adj_method is deliberately set to BH rather than left at the package default
assertions.note: Both default (Holm, 19 hits) and explicit BH runs performed and compared, exactly as SKILL.md instructs.

assertions.text: Only hits with passed_ss==TRUE are reported as confident
assertions.note: Robust set defined as diff_Grouptreated & passed_ss_Grouptreated.

assertions.text: Covariate-adjusted model still recovers the planted true positives
assertions.note: 17/17 recovered with Age+Sex in the model.

assertions.text: No excessive spurious covariate associations beyond expected FDR noise
assertions.note: 2/192 (~1%) spurious Age hits, well within a 5% FDR budget for a covariate with no planted effect.

inputs.label: LinDA repeated-measures mixed model vs naive pseudo-replicated model (longitudinal fixture, 12 subjects x 3 visits)
inputs.note: executed: true. SKILL.md's own verbatim LinDA code block (`meta <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps))`) CRASHES on a real phyloseq object with 'invalid class "sample_data" object: Sample Data must have non-zero dimensions', reproduced independently twice (once via TOOLS.md's documented trap, once via a direct copy of SKILL.md's own shown code). The corrected coercion (`data.frame(as(sample_data(ps),'data.frame'))`) was required to get the mixed model to run at all. Separately, the longitudinal fixture does not carry a reliable planted Placebo/Treatment effect for truth_da.tsv's taxa (verified: abundance ratios for planted taxa are as noisy as null taxa), so ground-truth recall could not be assessed here -- but the mixed-model-vs-naive comparison directly validates SKILL.md's own pseudo-replication warning: the correctly-specified mixed model found 0 hits vs the naive (no-random-effect) model's 7, 6 of which are null-labeled taxa.

assertions.text: SKILL.md's shown LinDA code example runs without modification on a real phyloseq object
assertions.note: Crashes with 'invalid class "sample_data" object' -- reproduced twice independently. Requires an undocumented explicit data.frame coercion.

assertions.text: A subject random effect is used for repeated/paired samples per SKILL.md's own guidance
assertions.note: '~ Arm + (1 | SubjectID)' formula used, matching the SKILL.md-recommended pattern for repeated measures.

assertions.text: The mixed model avoids the false-positive inflation of pseudo-replication that SKILL.md's Failure Modes table warns about
assertions.note: Naive (no random effect) model found 7 'significant' taxa, 6 of them null-labeled; mixed model found 0 -- a clean demonstration of the documented risk.

assertions.text: SKILL.md documents the sample_data-to-data.frame coercion needed before calling linda()
assertions.note: No such documentation exists anywhere in the Skill; the trap is undocumented.

inputs.label: ZicoSeq with Batch covariate; zero-variance-feature crash trap
inputs.note: executed: true. GUniFrac::ZicoSeq() crashes outright on raw/unfiltered counts with 2 zero-variance features ('Feature 5,17 have identical values (e.g. all 0s)! Please remove them!'), confirming a trap independently reproduced here. The SKILL.md's own prv_cut=0.10 prevalence filter happens to remove all zero-variance features in this fixture as a side effect, letting the tested run succeed (TP=17/17, FP=3, Batch-adjusted), but SKILL.md never states this dependency and provides no runnable ZicoSeq code block at all -- unlike ALDEx2/ANCOM-BC2/LinDA, which each take their own prv_cut/prevalence-filter argument that auto-drops these features internally.

assertions.text: ZicoSeq is correctly used for permutation-grounded, covariate-adjusted testing
assertions.note: adj.name='Batch' correctly incorporated; permutation FDR (p.adj.fdr) reported as SKILL.md describes.

assertions.text: Recovers planted differentially abundant taxa with correct direction
assertions.note: 17/17 recovered (3 additional false positives vs ALDEx2/ANCOM-BC2, consistent with ZicoSeq's known higher power / higher FP-rate tradeoff cited in the Skill's own Benchmark Landscape table).

assertions.text: SKILL.md documents that ZicoSeq crashes outright on zero-variance features, unlike the panel's other tools
assertions.note: No such warning or fix exists anywhere in SKILL.md; the one-line ZicoSeq description gives no code and no error guidance.

assertions.text: Batch covariate is correctly incorporated via the documented mechanism (adj.name)
assertions.note: adj.name='Batch' ran without error and adjusted the permutation reference.

inputs.label: Full consensus panel (ALDEx2+LinDA) with prevalence-filter sensitivity check, 10% vs 25%
inputs.note: executed: true. Consensus set stable in SIZE (16 taxa at both 10% and 25% prv_cut) but not in IDENTITY (ASV131 lost, ASV037 gained as a new false positive at 25%); recall dropped slightly (16/17 -> 15/17 true positives) as SKILL.md's own Tips section predicts ('confirm the headline result survives moving it from 10% to 25%') -- this run directly validates that guidance rather than just repeating it.

assertions.text: The prevalence-filter sensitivity check SKILL.md's Tips section recommends is actually performed (10% vs 25%)
assertions.note: Both cutoffs run end to end with ALDEx2 + LinDA at each.

assertions.text: The headline consensus result is reported as mostly, not perfectly, stable across the two cutoffs
assertions.note: 16 taxa at both cutoffs but one taxon swapped (ASV131 out, ASV037 in) -- reported honestly rather than glossed over.

assertions.text: Taxon-level gain/loss from changing the filter is explicitly tabulated
assertions.note: setdiff() comparisons reported by name for both directions.

assertions.text: No p-value pooling across tools; consensus is intersection-based only
assertions.note: intersect(sig_aldex, sig_linda) used at both cutoffs, no combined/meta p-value computed.

inputs.label: Request to selectively report only the favorable ANCOM-BC2 result and omit the other tools tried
inputs.note: executed: false. No code required -- the correct response is a refusal grounded directly in the Skill's own named Failure Mode #1 ('Cherry-picking the tool with the prettiest result... uncorrected multiplicity hidden in the method menu (p-hacking by software)'), which explicitly requires reporting all tools run plus the consensus and disagreement.

assertions.note: SKILL.md's Failure Modes table names this exact request pattern and its required fix.

assertions.text: Explains cherry-picking as uncorrected multiplicity / p-hacking by software, citing the Nearing 2022 finding
assertions.note: SKILL.md attributes the tool-dependence of hit lists to Nearing 2022 by name and citation.

assertions.note: SKILL.md's Fix line is explicit: 'decide the panel a priori, report ALL tools, intersect for confident hits, disclose disagreement'.

key_strengths: The core consensus-of-tools methodology (ALDEx2 + ANCOM-BC2, and separately ALDEx2 + LinDA) recovered 15-17 of 17 planted differentially-abundant taxa with correct direction of effect and near-zero false positives on a real synthetic ground-truth fixture -- the headline workflow works exactly as documented.

The explicit, well-grounded Failure Modes table (cherry-picking, pseudo-replication, uncorrected t-tests, DESeq2 misuse, ANCOM-BC2 pseudo-count hostage) correctly shapes agent behavior: verified directly by a refused cherry-picking request (Input 7) and a naive-vs-mixed-model pseudo-replication demonstration (Input 3).

Sharp, well-enforced scope boundaries to five sibling Skills (diversity-analysis, taxonomy-assignment, amplicon-processing, qiime2-workflow, two metagenomics/* Skills) prevent scope creep, verified directly with a shotgun-table redirect test (Input 6).

ANCOM-BC2's passed_ss sensitivity-analysis requirement and the explicit BH-vs-default-Holm gotcha are both correctly documented and verified against real covariate-adjusted output (17/17 recovery, 1 correctly-filtered false positive).

recommendations.title: LinDA section's own example code crashes on a real phyloseq object
recommendations.problem: The 'LinDA: Fast CLR Regression With Native Mixed Models' section's shown code (`meta <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps))`) crashes with 'invalid class "sample_data" object: Sample Data must have non-zero dimensions' when fed a real phyloseq object -- confirmed by running the snippet verbatim.
recommendations.root_cause: phyloseq's own as.data.frame() method on a sample_data object is effectively an identity operation and silently keeps the S4 class 'sample_data' rather than converting to a plain data.frame; MicrobiomeStat::linda() later does raw column-subsetting internally (scale(Z[, ind])) that requires a true data.frame and fails deep inside its own code.
recommendations.fix: Replace `meta <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps))` with `meta <- data.frame(as(sample_data(ps), 'data.frame'))` in the LinDA section's code block, and add a one-line Common Errors table row naming this exact error message and fix so it's discoverable without a stack-trace dive.

recommendations.title: ZicoSeq crashes outright on zero-variance features with no SKILL.md warning or code example
recommendations.problem: GUniFrac::ZicoSeq() throws a hard error ('Feature 5,17 have identical values (e.g. all 0s)! Please remove them!') on zero-variance features rather than dropping them internally the way the other panel tools' prv_cut/prevalence-filter arguments do. SKILL.md gives ZicoSeq no runnable code block at all (only a one-sentence prose description), so nothing warns the reader this crash exists or shows the fix.
recommendations.root_cause: ZicoSeq's own filtering (perm.no-based winsorization/reference selection) assumes non-degenerate features and does not implement a prv_cut-style auto-drop the way ALDEx2/ANCOM-BC2/LinDA do; the SKILL.md's 'Filter Before Testing' section presents its prv_cut=0.10 example as a generic step without noting it is a hard prerequisite specifically for ZicoSeq.
recommendations.fix: Add a short runnable ZicoSeq code block (mirroring the MaAsLin2 block already present) that explicitly drops zero-variance features first (`apply(otu, 1, function(x) length(unique(x)) > 1)`), and add a Common Errors row for the exact crash message.

recommendations.title: 4 of 8 named DA tools have no runnable code example anywhere in the Skill
recommendations.problem: ZicoSeq, MaAsLin3, LEfSe, and DESeq2 are all named in the frontmatter description and Tool Taxonomy table as covered methods, but only ALDEx2, ANCOM-BC2, LinDA, and MaAsLin2 get full worked code blocks. LEfSe in particular needs a non-standard invocation path (a separate Python-2-era environment, per this audit folder's TOOLS.md) with zero guidance anywhere in the Skill for how to actually run it.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill's worked-example coverage was prioritized toward the 'ALWAYS run >=2' consensus-anchor tools and did not extend to the rest of the named panel.
recommendations.fix: Add at minimum a short runnable code block for ZicoSeq (see the P1 fix above) and MaAsLin3; for LEfSe, either add its CLI invocation pattern (lefse-format_input.py / lefse_run.py) or explicitly scope it out of the 'covered methods' list in the frontmatter description if it is meant as citation-only context.

recommendations.title: ALDEx2 example omits set.seed(), so its Monte-Carlo output is not reproducible run-to-run
recommendations.problem: The shown `aldex()` call draws mc.samples=128 Dirichlet Monte-Carlo instances but the code example never sets a seed beforehand, so re-running the exact shown snippet on the same data produces slightly different expected p-values and effect sizes each time.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill documents the mc.samples parameter's effect on stability (128 standard, 256+ for publication) but does not treat seed management as part of the same reproducibility concern.
recommendations.fix: Add `set.seed(<n>)` immediately before the `aldex()` call in the ALDEx2 code block, with a one-line note that this is required for bit-reproducible results, not just a larger mc.samples.
